title: Go to the Grave in All Thy Glorious Prime
description: Go to the Grave in All Thy Glorious Prime in Tonic Solfa to ELLERS, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 408, “Death in Manhood”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Tens (10.10.10.10) (10.10.10.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ELLERS; any other Tens (10.10.10.10) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Go to the grave in all thy glo-rious prime, In full ac-tiv-i-ty of zeal and power: A Chris-tian can-not die be-fore his time; The Lord's ap-point-ment is the ser-vant's hour.

lines: Go to the grave in all thy glorious prime,
In full activity of zeal and power:
A Christian cannot die before his time;
The Lord's appointment is the servant's hour.
Go to the grave; at noon from labor cease;
Rest on thy sheaves, thy harvest work is done;
Come from the heat of battle, and in peace,
Soldier, go home; with thee the field is won.
Go to the grave, for there thy Saviour lay,
In death's embraces, ere he rose on high;
And all the ransomed, by that narrow way,
Pass to eternal life beyond the sky.
Go to the grave, — no, to thy home above;
Be thy pure spirit present with the Lord,
Where thou for faith and hope hast perfect love,
And open vision for the written word.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ELLERS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
